doc.title: Javon Jackson interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 3, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Making the call to cancel engagements
summary: Monk describes a venue asking him to decide; Jackson says he informed musicians, e.g. the Saratoga date, and clubs were closed anyway.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Yeah. I had one experience where the venue — it is a fairly small venue — and the person called me up and asked me, “Well what do you think? Do you want to do it?” And it was the first time that had happened, I think about the only time. And I wasn’t sure what to say because I was unprepared to make the call myself and I had four other people that I was basically — would have been affected by it. Did you have to cancel anything yourself, or have the opportunity?
Did I have the opportunity to cancel any gig that I had?

Well there were a lot of my gigs I got to call and then I would inform the musicians. I mean actually today one of the band members said, “I guess Saratoga” — Saratoga was going to be June 25 or 27 of this year, at the end of this month. And they said, “I guess © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-

Saratoga is cancelled, right?” I said, “Yes.” So sometimes I didn’t make the call because I just assumed that everyone thought everything has been cancelled. But then some people were still holding out with some sense of hope that it would occur. But I’ve made some calls but mostly it wasn’t going to happen so — all the clubs have been closed. So there’s no reason for somebody to be saying are we going to be playing at this club, because all the clubs are closed. So it means there’s no concert, or no performance.
